product.olivetti-m10.summary: 1983 portable with an OKI 80C85, 8-32 KB of battery-backed RAM, a 240x64 LCD and built-in BASIC, TEXT, TELCOM and ADDRSS. An experimental pilot is available.
product.olivetti-m10.history: Contemporary press (MCmicrocomputer 27, February 1984) attributes the M10 and the Tandy Model 100 to Kyocera manufacture; they are related platforms, not aliases. The international ROM holds English, German, Italian and French keyboard layouts chosen by board jumpers. BluMach runs the 32 KB system ROM to the menu and BASIC and keeps RAM and clock in the machine folder.
product.olivetti-m10.warning: EXPERIMENTAL PILOT: the menu, BASIC, the four RAM sizes, the keyboard, the clock and warm restarts are validated. Timing is approximate. Cassette, RS-232C, printer, bar-code reader and modem are not modelled, and the buzzer has no host sound output yet.
product.olivetti-m10.creation.model: M10 portable (1983) with LCD, keyboard, clock and battery-backed RAM
product.olivetti-m10.creation.note: The firmware's cold start sets the clock to 01 Jan 1900; set DATE$ and TIME$ in BASIC once and the machine folder keeps them. After 10 minutes waiting for a command the M10 switches itself off: use Reset, the equivalent of the power switch.
product.olivetti-m10.creation.help.clock: Applies only when the machine has no saved clock yet. Host time also keeps the clock running while the machine is closed.
product.olivetti-m10.technical.cpu_bus: OKI MSM80C85A at 2.4576 MHz. An OKI MSM81C55 at B0h-BFh provides ports A-C and the 14-bit timer; E0h-EFh reads the key matrix and writes the control latch.
product.olivetti-m10.technical.memory_ma: ROM at 0000h-7FFFh; RAM grows down from FFFFh in 8 KB steps (E000h, C000h, A000h, 8000h). Unpopulated addresses read FFh (assumption).
product.olivetti-m10.technical.video: Ten HD44102CH drivers at F0h-FFh, selected by 81C55 PA0-PA7 and PB0-PB1; A0 selects data or instruction. The panel shows 240 of the 250 addressable columns.
product.olivetti-m10.technical.keyboard: Nine rows strobed by PA0-PA7 and PB0 with one diode per key. PC keys follow the physical positions of the USA-ASCII M10 keyboard; PASTE is F9, LABEL F10, PRINT Print Screen, BREAK Pause, GRPH Alt and NUM Insert. CAPS LOCK latches.
product.olivetti-m10.technical.rtc: uPD1990AC on PA0-PA4, PC0 and STB from the E0h latch; TP at 256 Hz drives RST 7.5. The chip keeps no year: the firmware keeps it in RAM and always prints 19xx.
product.olivetti-m10.technical.buzzer_po: Buzzer gate PB5 AND (PB2 OR 81C55 TIMER OUT) from the service manual. P.C.S. on PB4 switches the machine off after 10 idle minutes; the RAM is kept.
product.olivetti-m10.technical.firmware: Local 32 KB international ROM. Cold or warm start is decided by the RAM signature at F5F0h; cold start sets the clock from a table to 01 Jan 00:00:00.
product.olivetti-m10.technical.implement: An engineering note records how the CoreMach M10 firmware probe became this machine: CPU, LCD driver, clock and 81C55 components written from primary data books, and the board wiring from the service manual.
product.olivetti-m10.technical.status: Validated: menu and BASIC sign-on as in the operations guide, bytes free for 8/16/24/32 KB, typing in BASIC, TP period, warm restart keeping a BASIC program and the date, auto power-off and BEEP edges.
product.olivetti-m10.technical.limitatio: Instruction timing is per instruction, not per bus phase; LCD BUSY time is approximate. No host audio for the buzzer. Cassette, UART, printer, bar-code reader, modem, low-battery TRAP and the 81C55 RAM are not modelled.
product.olivetti-m10.source.service_manu: M10 Manuale generale per l'assistenza, 4100230 N (0), October 1983
